title: Transitivity of the structural dualizing counit
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-trf-admissibility], with $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $a_Y:Y\to s$ and $a_X=a_Yf$ be the structure maps, and use their specified constructible exceptional adjunctions. Set $\omega_X=Ra_X^!A_s$ and $\omega_Y=Ra_Y^!A_s$ as in [def-trf-dualizing-complex]. Let $i_f:\omega_X\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!\omega_Y$ be the inverse of the canonical isomorphism of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition], namely the component at $A_s$ of the conjugate exceptional composition comparison of [def-trf-admissibility]. Define
$$\tau_f=\varepsilon_{f,\omega_Y}\circ Rf_!i_f:Rf_*\omega_X=Rf_!\omega_X\longrightarrow\omega_Y,$$
and let $t_X:Ra_{X!}\omega_X\to A_s$, $t_Y:Ra_{Y!}\omega_Y\to A_s$ be the structure-adjunction counits. Then
$$t_Y\circ Ra_{Y!}\tau_f=t_X$$
as maps $Ra_{X!}\omega_X\to A_s$, after precomposing the left side with the specified compact-support composition isomorphism $Ra_{X!}\omega_X\cong Ra_{Y!}Rf_!\omega_X$.

source.place: Step 3, proof of (a): “epsilon_{a_Y} Ra_{Y!} tau_f = epsilon_{a_X} (the counit of a_X=a_Yf is the pasted counit)”

proof.text: Work throughout in $\mathcal D_T=D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ with the one fixed finite coefficient ring $A$. Write $L=Rf_!$, $R=Rf^!$, $M=Ra_{Y!}$, $S=Ra_Y^!$, $H=Ra_{X!}$ and $T=Ra_X^!$. The specified adjunctions are $L\dashv R$, $M\dashv S$ and $H\dashv T$, by [def-trf-admissibility]. Denote the specified compact-support composition isomorphism by $\alpha:ML\xrightarrow{\sim}H$. This is the inverse direction to the precomposition isomorphism in the conclusion. By [def-trf-dualizing-complex], $TA_s=\omega_X$ and $SA_s=\omega_Y$. The canonical isomorphism of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition] identifies $RSA_s$ with $TA_s$; its inverse is the given $i_f$. All these functors and adjunctions have the stated constructible finite-Tor domains; no adjunction on the whole unbounded category is used.

source.place: Step 3, structural-counit identity; notation for its specified adjunctions

proof.text: Form the composite adjunction $ML\dashv RS$ of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Its counit at $N\in\mathcal D_s$ is the explicitly pasted map $$e_N=\varepsilon_{a_Y,N}\circ M(\varepsilon_{f,SN}):MLRSN\longrightarrow N.$$ This applies to the actual two specified adjunctions, without replacing the independently specified adjunction $H\dashv T$ by the composite adjunction.

source.place: Tags 0DV0 (lemma-compose-counits) and 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints); applied to the specified constructible adjunctions

proof.text: Conjugate $\alpha:ML\to H$ between $H\dashv T$ and $ML\dashv RS$, obtaining $j:T\to RS$. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], conjugation preserves isomorphisms and takes inverses to inverses. The normalization of exceptional composition in [def-trf-admissibility] therefore identifies $j_{A_s}$ with the specified $i_f$: the comparison in the opposite direction is the conjugate of $\alpha^{-1}$. Apply the transpose characterization of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] with $L_1=H$, $R_1=T$, $L_2=ML$, $R_2=RS$, and both vertical functors identity. It says exactly that the transpose of $j_N$ under $ML\dashv RS$ is $\varepsilon_{a_X,N}\circ\alpha_{TN}$. Written using the counit $e$ from Step 2, this is $$e_N\circ ML(j_N)=\varepsilon_{a_X,N}\circ\alpha_{TN}:MLTN\longrightarrow N.$$ Thus the compatibility is an application of the cited mate statement, rather than a claim that arbitrary chosen right-adjoint isomorphisms preserve counits.

Evaluate the identity of Step 3 at $N=A_s$. Substituting $j_{A_s}=i_f$ and the formula for $e_{A_s}$ from Step 2, then using functoriality of $M$, gives $$\begin{aligned}t_Y\circ M(\tau_f)\circ\alpha_{\omega_X}^{-1}&=\varepsilon_{a_Y,A_s}\circ M(\varepsilon_{f,SA_s})\circ ML(i_f)\circ\alpha_{TA_s}^{-1}\\&=e_{A_s}\circ ML(j_{A_s})\circ\alpha_{TA_s}^{-1}\\&=\varepsilon_{a_X,A_s}\circ\alpha_{TA_s}\circ\alpha_{TA_s}^{-1}\\&=t_X.\end{aligned}$$ Here the first equality is precisely the definition $\tau_f=\varepsilon_{f,\omega_Y}\circ L(i_f)$ in the item; the last equality cancels an isomorphism and its inverse. The domain is $H\omega_X=Ra_{X!}\omega_X$, and $\alpha_{\omega_X}^{-1}$ is exactly the precomposition required by the statement. Properness is used in the statement to label $L\omega_X$ also as $Rf_*\omega_X$; the calculation itself retains compact supports throughout, so it does not impose properness of $a_X$ or $a_Y$.
